newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close mixed, Olivetti sinks.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close mixed, Olivetti sinks.

text.p: Italian shares closed mixed on Monday with selected banking and insurance stocks making strong gains while Olivetti resumed its slide after news broke that the group's chief executive was under preliminary investigation.
The all-share mibtel index closed 0.31 percent higher while the blue-chip mib30 index finished 0.37 down. Turnover was up sharply from Friday with 708.9 billion lire worth of shares changing hands.
Apart from Olivetti, which last traded at 516 lire before trading was suspended -- representing a drop of 9.84 percent since Friday's close -- Fiat and Montedison also slipped.

News that Olivetti's CEO could become the target of an investigation centred on the company's first half results hit a market which was still shaken by the company's decision to delay a meeting with analysts in Milan and London.

Investors shaved 1.67 percent off the value of Fiat shares, which ended at 4,245 lire, amid fears that the group's first-half results would reflect the sluggish performance of the European car market.
Telecom Italia Mobile shares took a dive, falling 3.38 percent to 2,888 lire, amid concerns over whether it can quickly switch subscribers from its analogue network to its higher-value GSM system.
Shares in Compart, formerly known as Ferruzzi, rose 3.3 percent, driven by an apparent wave of optimism over the group's future.

Shares in Italian financier Carlo De Benedetti's holding companies CIR and Cofide also took a battering while food group Parmalat rose on a bout of short-covering after last week's losses over a botulism scare.
